title: Function Arcade
subtitle: Eight machines in the pool — six drawn each run. Tap, type, match, and sort before the clock kills you.
description: A mixed-mechanic arcade run through Chapter 1. Every run draws six rounds from a pool of eight, so answer positions never settle in.

rounds.prompt: Shift $f(x) = x^2$ right 3 and down 2. Which equation lands the shot?
rounds.hint: Inside the parentheses moves the opposite way you expect.
rounds.explain: Clean hit! $x - 3$ slides it right 3, and the $-2$ outside drops it 2.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! $x + 3$ shifts LEFT. Right 3 needs $x - 3$ inside, down 2 needs $-2$ outside.

rounds.prompt: Every graph that passes the vertical line test also has an inverse function.
rounds.explain: Boom — false. The vertical line test only proves it is a function; you need the HORIZONTAL line test for an inverse.
rounds.missExplain: Careful — vertical line test means it IS a function. One-to-one (horizontal line test) is what buys you an inverse.

rounds.prompt: Let $f(x) = 2x^2 - 5$. Fire off the value of $f(-3)$.
rounds.hint: Square before you multiply — the negative disappears.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! Square first: $(-3)^2 = 9$. Then $2(9) - 5 = 13$, not $-23$.

rounds.prompt: Connect each parent function to the feature that gives it away.
rounds.explain: Locked in! Each parent has one signature feature — that is your fastest identification tool.
rounds.missExplain: Almost — remember $\frac{1}{x}$ owns the asymptote pair, while $\sqrt{x}$ is the one with a restricted domain.

rounds.prompt: Select EVERY function whose domain is all real numbers.
rounds.hint: Only radicals and denominators can block inputs here.
rounds.explain: Clean sweep! Polynomials and absolute value accept every input; the radical needs $x \ge 1$ and the fraction dies at $x = -5$.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! $\sqrt{x - 1}$ needs $x \ge 1$ and $\frac{2}{x + 5}$ breaks at $x = -5$, so only the polynomial and the absolute value survive.

rounds.prompt: Sort each function by its symmetry.
rounds.hint: Test $f(-x)$: same means even, opposite means odd.
rounds.explain: Checkpoint cleared! Even powers only means even; odd powers only means odd; mix them and you get neither.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! $x^2 + x$ mixes an even and an odd power, so $f(-x)$ is neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$.

rounds.prompt: Line these values up from smallest to largest.
With $f(x) = x^2 + 1$ and $g(x) = x - 3$, what is $(f \circ g)(x)$?
rounds.explain: Clean hit! $(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$, so every $x$ in $f$ becomes $x - 3$.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! That is $g(f(x))$. Composition order matters: $f \circ g$ drops $g$ INTO $f$.
